title: Roots Beneath the Quarantine Wall
paras: At dawn on Bellweather Island, sea lavender seems to [[enchant|enchant]] even our usually impatient surveyor, who kneels beside its violet flowers. We have come to record the vegetation surrounding a seventeenth-century quarantine station. Its surviving enclosure can be walked in its [[entirety|entirety]] within twenty minutes, although brambles conceal the northern gate and roots have displaced several limestone steps.

The harbour ledger describes a [[bloc|bloc]] of merchants who financed the station after [[plague|plague]] reached neighbouring ports. Their correspondence reveals [[bottom-line|bottom-line]] calculations: keeping infected vessels offshore promised fewer interruptions to trade. Beside the ruined storehouse, a brick-lined pit served for the [[incineration|incineration]] of contaminated bedding; this morning, its shallow depression holds rainwater and three motionless damselfly larvae.

Along the eastern wall, [[indigenous|indigenous]] grasses [[mingle|mingle]] with fennel descended, perhaps, from plants once cultivated by the station's attendants. That possibility remains unproven: seeds could equally have arrived with later visitors. It would be [[reckless|reckless]] to pull apart the masonry in search of botanical evidence, since nesting lizards occupy its fissures. Instead, we photograph each patch against a numbered scale.

By midday, our map shows denser vegetation around the former burning pit than on the exposed courtyard, but soil samples will be needed before we can explain the contrast. We [[aspire|aspire]] to reconstruct how confinement altered this small island without treating every leaf as historical testimony. As we leave, a damselfly settles on the ledger's pencilled copy: the old boundary now shelters lives it was never designed to contain.
zh: 黎明时分，在贝尔韦瑟岛上，就连我们那位平日缺乏耐心的测绘员，似乎也被补血草迷住了，跪下身来细看它紫色的花朵。我们此行是为了记录一座十七世纪检疫站周围的植被。沿着现存围墙走完一圈只需二十分钟，不过，荆棘遮住了北门，树根也顶歪了几级石灰岩台阶。
港口账簿记载，鼠疫传到邻近港口后，一个商人联盟出资建造了这座检疫站。他们的通信透露出对最终利润的盘算：让染疫船只停留在近海，有望减少贸易中断。在仓库废墟旁，一处砖砌坑曾用于焚烧受污染的寝具；今天早晨，这个浅坑积着雨水，里面有三只一动不动的豆娘幼虫。
沿着东墙，本土禾草与茴香交错生长；这些茴香或许是当年检疫站工作人员所种植物的后代。但这种可能性尚未得到证实：种子同样可能由后来的访客带来。为了寻找植物学证据而拆动砌石，实属鲁莽，因为石缝中栖居着筑巢的蜥蜴。我们转而在每片植被旁放置带编号的标尺，拍照记录。
到了中午，我们绘制的地图显示，旧焚烧坑周围的植被比无遮蔽的庭院更加茂密，但要解释这一差异，还需要采集土壤样本。我们希望重建隔离措施改变这座小岛的过程，却不愿把每一片叶子都当作历史证据。离开时，一只豆娘停在用铅笔抄录的账簿副本上：这道古老的边界，如今庇护着当初建造它时从未打算容纳的生命。

q.s: The merchants expected offshore quarantine to help protect their trading income.
q.why: 商人预计近海隔离能减少贸易中断。

q.s: The researchers have used genetic testing to investigate the fennel's origins.
q.why: 文中未说明是否用过基因检测。

q.s: The map shows denser vegetation in the exposed courtyard than around the former burning pit.
q.why: 地图显示焚烧坑周围植被更茂密。
